title: Armature Catalog Documentation 2.0
$comment: The documentation model of a catalog: what a unit may say ABOUT itself, for people. Modelled on the documentation fields of OpenAPI 3.1 (info, summary/description, externalDocs, tags, deprecated) and JSON Schema (description), with the same rule as both: documentation never changes what a document denotes. Every field defined here is inert for --validate, --d1 and D2–D6 (SPECIFICATION §10.2: a field no conforming implementation reads is a comment). Only --document and --lint read them. The catalog grammar (armature-catalog-unit.schema.json) declares the same fields at each site it documents; this schema is what --document validates the extracted documentation against. Nothing here is a site of its own.

summary.$comment: One line of plain text, at most 120 characters. What the unit IS, for an index row or a table cell. Not CommonMark.

description.$comment: CommonMark. What the unit MEANS and how to use it. It must not restate a fact the definition carries — types, defaults, shapes, laws are rendered from the definition, so a description that repeats them can only drift from them.

url.$comment: An absolute URI, or a path relative to the repository root. The renderer rewrites a root-relative path so that it resolves from wherever the page is written; on stdout it stays root-relative.

kind.$comment: Lets the renderer group links. `reference_implementation` is the modeling_x.py, the engine file, the kernel: what the contract abstracts, never what it depends on.

external_docs.$comment: OpenAPI allows one externalDocs object; a primitive routinely has several sources (the paper, the reference code, the discussion that fixed a convention), hence a list.

tags.$comment: Editorial, cross-cutting grouping. Contract namespaces (attention.*, residual.*) already group by structure; a tag groups by a property that cuts across namespaces. A tag a unit cites should be declared by the base (lint).

deprecation.$comment: A deprecated unit keeps its identity and its meaning (§8.2): deprecation is advice to authors, not a change of denotation. OpenAPI's boolean is replaced by an object because the useful fact is what to use instead.

superseded_by.$comment: Another argument of the same contract.

value_descriptions.$comment: One description per enum value, keyed by the value as a string. Only on an argument (or record field) of enum type; every key must be one of its declared values (checked by --document). OpenAPI has no equivalent and resorts to x-enum-descriptions.

unit_documentation.$comment: What a contract, an axis or a precision role may say about itself. The fields sit directly in the unit's `definition`, beside `note`; this object names the set so a tool can extract and check it.

base_documentation.$comment: OpenAPI's `info` object, minus `version`: a catalog has no global version (§8.2), identity is carried contract by contract. `tags` DECLARES the tags units may cite, as OpenAPI's top-level tags array does.

argument_documentation.$comment: On an argument and on each field of a record argument.

element_documentation.$comment: On every other documented site of a contract: a value port, a parameter or constant slot, a state port, a payload component, a state operation, a state rule, a partition, a logical-cost entry, a domain transform, an alias rule. One field: the site's other facts are already declared and rendered.
